title: Government Incorporates Mexican Steel into the National Content of Public Works
author: La Redacción
content:
_This article by La Redacción originally appeared in the[August 31, 2026
edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/08/31/economia/gobierno-
incorpora-acero-mexicano-al-contenido-nacional-de-obras-publicas), Mexico's
premier left wing daily newspaper._

**Mexico City**. For the first time, the federal government incorporated
Mexican steel into the calculation of national content in public works, in
order to strengthen the Mexican industry of this material. The Anticorruption
and Good Governance Secretariat (SABG) published today in the Official Gazette
of the Federation (DOF) an accord that reforms the rules of national content
in public contracting to strengthen the country's national content and
production in government public works. This is done through the integration of
domestically manufactured steel materials, used in construction, into the
calculation of the percentage of national content of projects.

The agency noted that the reform to these rules **" represents an important
advance"** in the execution of the **Accord for the Promotion of the Mexican
Steel Industry, signed this past April 29 by President Claudia Sheinbaum
Pardo** , which established various actions to promote the use of national
steel in public purchases, so that these become a tool to strengthen the
country's production and productive chains.

Until now, the SABG added, the determination of national content in public
works considered materials different from those used directly in construction,
as well as machinery and permanently installed equipment. **" With the new
rules, the value of national steel incorporated into infrastructure may also
be counted, expanding the possibilities for public spending to boost the
Mexican steel industry."**

## The Percentage of Steel Will Be Determined in Each Project

According to the new rules, the percentage of national steel will be
established for each project considering the availability of production in
Mexico, the required quality, delivery deadlines, and the specific
characteristics of the work. Thus, **" greater participation of the national
industry will be promoted without compromising the best contracting conditions
for the State, the technical and economic viability of the projects, or the
execution times of the infrastructure."**

The agency headed by Secretary Raquel Buenrostro noted in a statement that the
new provisions strengthen the verification of national content. Awarded
companies must present documentation proving compliance with the established
percentages, and the agencies and entities will verify, upon receiving the
materials, that these correspond to the requirements set out in each
contracting procedure.

> The Accord for the Promotion of the Mexican Steel Industry translates into
> concrete rules to take advantage of the State's purchasing power, strengthen
> national production, and give greater certainty and traceability to the use
> of Mexican steel in public infrastructure.
>
> — Anticorruption and Good Governance Secretariat (SABG)
